children: , the American memory-chip producer, fell about 4.2% to $985.93 at 10.55am EST on October 12 as Chinese rival CXMT's technology progress rattled memory-chip investors. According to the South China Morning Post, CXMT outlined advances in denser 4F DRAM and plans to launch server memory by year-end. The concern is straightforward: another credible supplier could eventually put pressure on the industry's rich pricing.

Micron's own outlook still packs a punch. The company forecast fiscal-first-quarter revenue of $61.5 billion, plus or minus $1.5 billion, with gross margin near 86%. That revenue midpoint represents roughly 13.4% growth from its $54.23 billion fourth-quarter result. The valuation picture adds tension: shares sit 27.27% above the $774.68 GF Value estimate, leaving investors paying a premium even after the selloff.

The real test for CXMT comes on the factory floor. Smaller memory cells can squeeze more capacity onto a wafer, but commercial success also requires reliable yields, customer approvals and meaningful shipment volumes. Investors should watch those milestones before assuming Micron's pricing power is cracking. Today's strong outlook supports the earnings story; tomorrow's additional supply could challenge it. At a premium valuation, that uncertainty carries weight.

title: Micron Stocks Sink 4.2% as CXMT Targets Server Memory
